Chapter 14INPUT

The Outer Circuit

Keep moving, and the edge of the city holds.

The seawall looks like a path. It is also the edge of the city, and edges have to be checked. Every walker, runner and cyclist on the seawall, and every person who cannot sleep and goes for a walk along the water at two in the morning, is checking it without knowing.

In Terminal City their movement is what keeps the edge in place. A person tracing the city's edge, again and again, holds that edge where it is. When the movement thins out, a stretch of path or shoreline can start to drift, or a lamp repeats itself farther around the bend than it should.

The Green Static scrambles the Circuit's signals around Stanley Park, and somewhere near Wreck Beach there is a gap it has never fully closed. The rule is the shortest one in the city.

The ruleKeep moving.

Terminal City is an original fictional mythology inspired by Vancouver’s geography, weather, wildlife, infrastructure, art, and electronic music. It makes no claim to historical, Indigenous, or religious tradition. Real places are used as settings; the operating system layered on them is invented.
